chapter: Fisher's band and Jack Laine's bands
title: Playing Milneburg camps and the attic stunt
summary: Brunies recalls playing at Milneburg with Fisher and Schilling, returning in white suits full of cinders, and slipping up into the attic during dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah, then I used to go out to Millen Boyd and blow the roofs off the... There's all tin roofs out there. And I'd get up there with fishing and shilling, sometime with Jacqueline. Well, shilling's different, isn't it? Yeah, shilling is still... I talked to him one day. Yeah. And we'd go out there in the morning, with white suits on, and come back with our white suits loaded with cinders. Oh, yeah. From Smokey Murray. And not only our pockets loaded with cinders, something else, too, you know. So, we all used to have a good time, and all used to say, well, where's Rich yet? He ain't in the band. Well, he said, you know, the band would strike up. I'd leave one in the band, a leader. Put him next to what I'm gonna do. You know, these big attics in them places out there with cross pieces and all like that. So, they played, different albums all like that, and all of a sudden it stopped. And I picked it up. And there was one way that... The trouble it was coming from when I was way up in the attic. That would be a dance band, would it? How big a band did you use? About 76, 79, 70. And, I'm telling you, one man just played two drums, you know.
